_comment: Editor UI metadata for MPC SOS Fade — labels, groups, plain-English descriptions, the 'essentials' (core) flag, conditional visibility (show_if), toggle option labels, and tuning guides. Read by the command-center scanner (strategies/python/<pkg>/<pkg>.meta.json) and overlaid onto the schema built from SosFadeConfig. UI ONLY: it never touches a trade decision or the source hash, so editing it needs no re-parity — but DO click Scan Strategies after editing. Param order here is the canonical UI order. Every show_if below was verified against the code, not assumed: exec_fvg_deep_only deliberately has NO condition (it still filters which FVGs qualify when Require FVG is off), and div_rsi_len/div_pivot_len have none either (they drive the divergence that ARMS the setup, which show_div does not gate — show_div only gates the veto and the live DIV flag).
edge: It fades exhaustion, but only after structure agrees. Price grabs liquidity (a sweep of a known high/low) or prints a momentum divergence at an extreme; a shift of structure (SOS) confirms the tide actually turned; then it waits for a DEEP pullback into the fib zone and buys/sells the imbalance left behind on a clean fib line. Nothing is chased — every entry is a resting limit into a retracement. The default is the deep-entry combo: arm on liquidity sweeps, require the gap to sit fully past 0.5, and re-price a deep gap to the nearest fib (0.618/0.702/0.786) rather than its own edge. That combo measured about +237% at PF 6.2 / 85% win / 13% max drawdown over ~2 years of gold at 84 trades. The other lever is the HTF bias filter, which currently does nothing (both set to Ignore): this bot shorted a +75% bull market and won, so shorts carry most of the profit. That concentration is the open question.

steps.label: 01 · Arm
steps.title: Something looks exhausted
steps.detail: A liquidity sweep runs stops past a known high/low — the default arming trigger. (An RSI divergence at an overbought/oversold extreme can arm it too, but that's off by default now.)

steps.label: 02 · SOS
steps.title: Structure confirms it
steps.detail: A shift of structure breaks the other way within the staleness window. Without this the setup is just a guess and it never arms.

steps.label: 03 · Zone
steps.title: Wait for the pullback
steps.detail: Price retraces DEEP into the 0.5–0.886 fib band of the SOS leg and a live fair-value gap sitting fully past 0.5 overlaps it. A deep gap enters at the nearest fib just shallower (0.618/0.702/0.786) rather than the gap's own edge; a shallow gap enters at its edge. Always a resting limit — never a chase.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Ladder out
steps.detail: Take 30% at TP1 and move the stop to breakeven, 40% at TP2 and move the stop to TP1, then trail the runner. The runner is where the money is made.

params.name: exec_arm_div
params.label: Arm on divergence
params.desc: Let an RSI divergence start a setup. OFF by default now — the default combo arms on liquidity sweeps instead. Divergence-armed setups skew heavily short (in a rising market, sell divergences outnumber buy divergences about 2 to 1). Turn it on to trade the divergence pool on its own, or alongside sweeps.

params.name: exec_arm_sweep
params.label: Arm on liquidity sweep
params.desc: Let a liquidity sweep (price running stops past a known high/low) start a setup. ON by default — it is the arming trigger for the current deep-entry combo (sweep-arm + deep-gaps-only + deep-gap→fib entry), which measured about +237% at PF 6.2 / 85% win / 13% max drawdown over ~2 years of gold at 84 trades. That result is the COMBO, not sweep-arm alone: pair it with the two Entry-zone deep toggles below. Sweep-arm with shallow gaps allowed is much weaker.

params.name: aplus_window
params.label: Arm → SOS timeout
params.desc: How long an armed setup waits for structure to confirm before it gives up. Default is 4320 minutes — 3 days. This is a staleness backstop, not a trigger: it only throws away setups whose confirmation never came.
guide: Only fresh confirmations count — fewer setups
Stale exhaustion can still trigger days later

params.name: exec_req_fvg
params.label: Require an FVG
params.desc: Whether a fair-value gap must overlap the fib zone for an entry to exist. On, the resting limit goes at the gap's near edge. Off, it falls back to a plain 0.618 limit — more trades, less confluence behind each one.

params.name: exec_fvg_deep_only
params.label: Deep gaps only
params.desc: Only count a gap that sits fully beyond the 0.5 retracement. ON by default — part of the deep-entry combo. Demands a deeper pullback, so you get a better price on fewer fills. Note this still filters gaps even when 'Require an FVG' is off — it changes which gap becomes the entry price.

params.name: exec_deep_fib
params.label: Deep gap → nearest fib
params.desc: When a qualifying gap floats deep in the zone (its near edge past 0.618), rest the limit at the nearest fib just shallower — 0.618 / 0.702 / 0.786 — instead of chasing the gap's own edge. ON by default: it recovers the deep setups that used to miss when price stalled at a fib and turned back before ever tapping the gap. A gap sitting on a fib, or shallower than 0.618, is unchanged.

params.name: exec_fvg_50
params.label: 0.5-straddling gap entry (not supported)
params.desc: Pine-only for now. In TradingView this qualifies a gap that STRADDLES the 0.5 line (its bottom below, its top above) and rests the limit at 0.5 itself — the least favourable of the entry methods, ranked last behind the deep-gap edge, the deep-fib re-price and the Sniper Zone. NOT ported to this bot — leave it OFF; turning it on has no effect on a lab run (and the Pine-parity check refuses an export taken with it on).

params.name: exec_htf_weekly
params.label: Weekly bias rule
params.desc: Require the weekly trend to agree, not oppose, or oppose the trade. One of: Ignore · Must agree · Must not oppose · Must oppose (reversal). Default Ignore, which means the bot has NO trend filter at all — that's why it happily shorted a bull market.
guide: Ignore = no filter, trade every setup
Must agree = only with the weekly trend

params.name: exec_htf_daily
params.label: Daily bias rule
params.desc: Same four options as the weekly rule, applied to the daily trend: Ignore · Must agree · Must not oppose · Must oppose (reversal). Both rules are checked, so a setup must satisfy each one that isn't set to Ignore.

params.name: exec_htf_exhaust_only
params.label: Fade exhaustion only
params.desc: Block a trade that would fade a FRESH higher-timeframe breakout — the theory being an exhausted move is worth fading but a breaking one isn't. Blocks longs into a fresh breakdown and shorts into a fresh breakout.

params.name: exec_htf_source
params.label: Exhaustion timeframe
params.desc: Which timeframe counts as a fresh breakout for the rule above: Weekly · Daily · Either. 'Either' is the strictest — a breakout on either timeframe blocks the trade.

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk per trade
params.desc: How much of the account balance each trade risks — this bot sizes ITSELF, so this is the sizing knob and the lab's Sizing Mode does not apply to it. It compounds: 5% means 5% of the balance at that trade. The default of 10% is the Pine's own and is aggressive; it's what makes the raw backtest numbers look enormous.
guide: Smaller swings, slower growth
Bigger swings — 10% is already aggressive

params.name: exec_sl_level
params.label: Stop level
params.desc: Which fib level the stop sits at, as a retracement of the SOS leg: 0.618 · 0.702 · 0.786 · 0.886 · 1.0, or Custom for any ratio in between. Default 0.886 = just past the deep edge of the entry band — the tested setting, with 8 years and 188 trades behind it. 1.0 = the leg's origin, the widest and structurally safest: the setup is only wrong once price takes out the level that created it. The three tighter levels risk less per trade but can place the stop on top of the entry, which balloons position size — they are not supported. Pick Custom to type a level the ladder doesn't have (0.9, say) — the box for it appears below.

params.name: exec_sl_custom
params.label: Custom stop level
params.desc: The exact retracement of the SOS leg to put the stop at, when Stop level is set to Custom. Anything above 0 and up to 1.0 — so 0.9, which the dropdown never offered, sits between the 0.886 default and the 1.0 leg origin. Typing 0.886 here is identical to picking 0.886 above, to the last decimal place, so switching to Custom changes nothing until you move the number. DEEPER (towards 1.0) is the safe direction: a wider stop, a smaller position, more room before the setup is wrong. SHALLOWER than 0.886 is the dangerous half — the entry is a resting limit inside the 0.5-0.886 band, so a stop above the fill either cancels the trade outright or leaves a stop distance so small the position size balloons. Turn Minimum stop distance on before going there. Note this level has no TradingView equivalent yet, so a run using it can't be checked against the chart.
guide: Tighter stop, bigger position, less room to be right
Wider stop, smaller position, closer to the leg origin

params.name: exec_sl_buf_tk
params.label: Stop buffer
params.desc: Extra room beyond the chosen stop level, so a wick that grazes the level doesn't take you out. 1 tick = $0.01 on gold.
guide: Stop sits exactly on the level
More room for wicks, wider risk per trade

params.name: exec_min_stop_mode
params.label: Minimum stop distance
params.desc: Refuse a setup whose stop lands too close to the entry. Position size is risk divided by stop distance, so a stop that collapses onto the entry does not risk less — it buys an enormous position that ordinary noise takes out, and price can travel straight past the stop inside one bar for a loss far bigger than the 1R you agreed to. '% of price' scales itself as gold runs 1,200 to 3,300. 'Fixed $' is one flat number at both ends of that range. 'x ATR(14)' is the only one that reacts to a quiet vs violent market at the same price. This is an entry filter and has nothing to do with the runner trail. Off is the historical default; turn it on for live trading.

params.name: exec_min_stop_val
params.label: Minimum stop floor
params.desc: The floor value, in the unit of the mode above: a percent in '% of price', dollars of price in 'Fixed $', a multiple in 'x ATR(14)'. Ignored when the mode is Off. Measured over 8 years of gold 15m: mild floors (0.10% / $1.50 / 0.5 ATR) refuse 3-6 of 188 trades and are slightly positive; harder floors (0.15%+ / $2.50+ / 1.0 ATR+) start eating winners.
guide: Almost nothing is refused
Refuses real trades, not just degenerate ones

params.name: exec_tp1_pct
params.label: TP1 size
params.desc: How much of the position comes off at the first target. Taking TP1 also moves the stop to breakeven, so this is the trade-off: bank early and de-risk, or keep size on for the runner.
guide: More size left for the runner
Bank more early, smaller runner

params.name: exec_tp2_pct
params.label: TP2 size
params.desc: How much comes off at the second target, which also drags the stop up to TP1. Whatever is left after TP1 and TP2 is the runner — and the runner makes more than 100% of this bot's net profit, so shrinking it is not free.
guide: Bigger runner
Bank more at TP2, smaller runner

params.name: exec_be_buf_tk
params.label: Breakeven buffer
params.desc: How far past entry the stop goes when TP1 moves it to breakeven. A buffer means a 'breakeven' stop actually banks a little instead of scratching.
guide: True breakeven
Locks in more, stopped out sooner

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the runner is trailed once TP2 is banked. Fixed step ratchets a fixed dollar distance behind price. Structure parks the stop at the last confirmed swing — it breathes with the trend but the swing lags, so a big run hands a lot back at the turn. Structure + % ratchet (default) uses the same swing anchor and then climbs it a percent at a time as price runs, which is what stops the give-back. The runner is where this strategy's money is, so this is the highest-leverage setting on the page.
guide: Fixed step — mechanical, worst on a multi-year price range
Structure + % ratchet — keeps ~53% of each run instead of ~43%

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: Structure trail buffer
params.desc: How far below the confirmed swing low (or above the swing high) the runner's stop sits, so an ordinary wick through the swing doesn't clip it. Used by both Structure modes; ignored in Fixed step.
guide: Tight to the swing — clipped by wicks
Wide of the swing — survives noise, gives back more

params.name: exec_trail_pct
params.label: Runner ratchet step
params.desc: How fast the runner's stop climbs off the swing anchor — one step of this size for every step of favourable move. A percent rather than a dollar amount on purpose: gold ran 1,500 to 3,400 over the backtest, so no fixed dollar step is right at both ends. Measured over 6.6 years of 15m gold, 1.0 lifted the share of each run actually banked from 43% to 53% on the same trades and the same drawdown.
guide: Below 0.5 — clips runners, costs real edge
Above 2.5 — barely binds, back to the plain structure trail

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step
params.desc: How tightly the runner's stop ratchets behind price once TP2 is done. Fixed-step mode only.
guide: Tighter trail — banks sooner, cuts runners short
Looser trail — lets winners breathe, gives back more

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: Where the stop jumps the moment TP2 fills, before the trail takes over. TP1 price is tight and can scratch the runner on the first pullback. Breakeven gives the runner the most room. One trail step behind sits in between.
guide: TP1 price — protects the gain, scratches runners
Breakeven — maximum room for the runner

params.name: exec_close_opp_sos
params.label: Close on opposite SOS
params.desc: Close an open trade early if structure shifts against it. Off by default — the ladder and the stop already manage the trade, and exiting on every structure flip cuts runners short.

params.name: show_div
params.label: Track divergence
params.desc: Master switch for the divergence veto and the live DIV confluence flag. Careful: turning this OFF does not stop divergences from arming setups — it only silences the veto and the flag.

params.name: div_rsi_len
params.label: RSI length
params.desc: Lookback for the RSI that finds divergences. 14 is the standard Wilder setting.
guide: Twitchier RSI, more divergences
Smoother RSI, fewer but cleaner

params.name: div_pivot_len
params.label: Pivot width
params.desc: How many bars either side of a high/low are needed to confirm it as a pivot. This is also the lag: a divergence can only be confirmed this many bars after the fact — by design, so it never repaints.
guide: Confirms sooner, more noise
Confirms later, only real pivots

params.name: div_valid_bars
params.label: Divergence shelf life
params.desc: How long a confirmed divergence keeps the veto/DIV flag alive before it's considered stale.
guide: Expires fast
Stays live longer

params.name: div_veto
params.label: Veto on extremes
params.desc: Block a setup when the opposite divergence is live, or when RSI is at an extreme — i.e. don't buy into a live sell-divergence.

params.name: exec_respect_veto
params.label: Obey the veto
params.desc: Whether execution actually honours the veto above. Two switches because the veto can be computed and shown while you test trading through it.

params.name: div_extreme_ob
params.label: Overbought line
params.desc: RSI at or above this counts as an extreme and vetoes longs.
guide: Vetoes longs more often
Only vetoes at a true extreme

params.name: div_extreme_os
params.label: Oversold line
params.desc: RSI at or below this counts as an extreme and vetoes shorts.
guide: Only vetoes at a true extreme
Vetoes shorts more often

params.name: exec_aplus
params.label: Trade A+ setups
params.desc: Trade the A+ reversal — the fade of a structure break, which is this bot's whole edge. Off, no A+ entry ever fires. The only reason to switch it off is to read another setup in isolation, which is what the separate B-LEG bot does.

params.name: exec_bleg
params.label: Trade B-Leg setups
params.desc: Trade the B-Leg setup — the late retrace of an SOS, which takes far longer to play out. OFF here by design: the A+ bot never places a B-leg order, and its own Pine ships it off. The separate B-LEG bot (mpc_bleg) is where it runs, so the two setups stay in their own runs and their trades can never be confused.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: Allow long trades. Longs are rare here (7 of 40 over 2 years) but they win 86% of the time — they aren't broken, there just aren't many buy divergences in a rising market.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: Allow short trades. Shorts are ~83% of this bot's trades and carry 89% of its profit.

params.name: exec_secondary
params.label: 1m re-entry
params.desc: Add the 1-minute sniper re-entry: after the 15m primary reaches breakeven and price falls back into the zone, a 1m shift of structure re-enters. Needs a RECENT window (the broker serves ~35 days of 1m). Rare — ~3 fires in 2 years.

params.name: exec_conf_sz
params.label: Sniper Zone entry (not supported)
params.desc: Pine-only for now. In TradingView this lets the Sniper Zone's 0.5–0.618 pocket act as a second entry confirmation on a leg with no qualifying FVG. NOT ported to this bot — leave it OFF; turning it on has no effect on a lab run (and the Pine-parity check refuses an export taken with it on).

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No late-day entries
params.desc: Refuse new entries in the last hours before the gold close, when liquidity thins out and spreads widen.

params.name: flat_by_close
params.label: Flat by close
params.desc: Close everything before the daily close instead of holding overnight. Off by default, and that was measured: over 6.5 months, OFF made $39,454 (PF 1.44) and ON made $19,813 (PF 1.25). Only 4 trades ever held overnight — all winners, making 70% of the profit — against $36.80 of total swap. Flatting early buys a smaller drawdown for half the profit.

params.name: flat_by_close_min
params.label: Flatten this early
params.desc: How many minutes before the daily close to force everything flat.
guide: Hold closer to the bell
Exit earlier, more of the close avoided

params.name: exec_scratch_r
params.label: Scratch band
params.desc: Reporting only — it never changes a trade. A closed trade landing within this much of breakeven is graded SCRATCH instead of a win or a loss. It matters because this bot scratches a lot: 17 of 40 trades finished near breakeven.
guide: Fewer trades called scratch
More near-breakeven trades called scratch

params.name: fill_model
params.label: Fill model
params.desc: How fills are priced. 'bar' = the Pine's own intrabar guess with zero costs (the parity mode). 'tick' = real Vantage bid/ask fills with measured spread, slippage, and swap — what a real backtest uses. Pick 'tick' for any number you'll trust.

params.name: account_profile
params.label: Account profile
params.desc: Whose costs to charge in tick mode. 'vantage_demo' is the backtest broker (zero commission, real Vantage swap) so results match the VANTAGE_XAUUSD TradingView feed. The puprime_* profiles are the live broker's tiers, kept for reference. Ignored in bar mode.

params.name: symbol
params.label: Broker symbol
params.desc: The MT5 symbol the tick pull requests. Vantage gold is 'XAUUSD' (no '.s' suffix — that was PU Prime). Ignored in bar mode.
